findings.title: Resolve the contradiction between envelope order and weapon execution order
findings.claim: The tick promises commands apply in envelope order, but folding them into ShipInput loses ordering between command kinds. With a full held laser, missileLaunch followed by laserCharge(false) reports both applied and fires the laser before launching.
findings.evidence: plan L1785 promises input order; plan L1819–L1822 validates against unchanged tactical state and folds commands; plan L1159–L1169 executes lock, charge/release, then launch. The reused handler has the same ordering at src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/weapons.ts:L64–L74. spec L158–L159 describes launch freezing the laser and subsequent charge commands being rejected.
findings.why: Command acknowledgements and combat effects do not follow the promised ordering. The last-wins decision for commands of one kind does not explain reordering different kinds.
findings.fix: Specify and implement cross-kind ordering explicitly. Preserve envelope order after same-kind coalescing, or state and justify the canonical-order deviation. Add tests for both launch/release orders and both lock/release orders, checking results and effects.

findings.title: Make the Missile key guard inspect a production-created missile
findings.claim: The new Missile key guard checks a handwritten object against its own handwritten keys. It does not inspect the missile produced by the launcher.
findings.evidence: plan L834–L836 assigns a literal to launched.missiles[0] immediately before checking its keys. Production construction is at plan L1205–L1212 and src/renderer/src/sim/tactical/missiles.ts:L15–L22.
findings.why: This passes independently of the production constructor and can miss newly initialized optional fields. It therefore does not provide the runtime field guard claimed by plan L21 and L35.
findings.fix: Create the missile through launchMissile or applyWeaponsInput, then assert its keys against the flatten inventory. Keep the existing flattened-length assertion.

findings.title: Dispose the interior when duel construction fails
findings.claim: createDuel allocates an interior before validating the tactical map and repair points, then throws without disposing that interior.
findings.evidence: plan L1697 allocates the interior; plan L1700, L1705 and L1708 can subsequently throw. src/renderer/src/sim/state.ts:L72–L84 establishes shared entity allocation and component cleanup; L92–L100 provides disposeSimState.
findings.why: A rejected seed or layout leaves allocated entity IDs and module-level component cells behind, and the caller receives no state it can dispose.
findings.fix: Wrap post-allocation construction in try/catch, call disposeSimState(interior) on failure, and rethrow. Validate the tactical map before allocating the interior where practical.
